components.css: .ds-fig{margin:0;max-width:20rem}.ds-fig svg{display:block;width:100%;height:auto;overflow:visible}.ds-fig .w path{fill:none;stroke:#111418;stroke-width:1.6;stroke-linejoin:miter}.ds-fig .g{stroke:#8892A0;stroke-width:1;stroke-dasharray:3 3;fill:none}.ds-fig .d{stroke:#0B5FA5;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.ds-fig .l text{font:400 11px 'Source Code Pro',ui-monospace,monospace;fill:#111418}.ds-fig .t text{fill:#0B5FA5}.ds-fig figcaption{margin-top:1rem;font:400 .8rem/1.5 'B612',system-ui,sans-serif;color:#4A5563}.ds-fig figcaption strong{color:#111418}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference){.ds-fig .w path{stroke-dasharray:1;stroke-dashoffset:1;animation:ds-draw 1.1s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) .15s forwards}.ds-fig .w path+path{animation-delay:.45s}}@keyframes ds-draw{to{stroke-dashoffset:0}}

narrative.overview:
The documentation is set as the part datasheet a hardware engineer already trusts. A claim is a row with its condition and its source; limits are stated as plainly as results. The page is white, the ink is near-black, hairline rules do the work that cards and fills do elsewhere, and a single blue marks what can be followed or measured. It is read at a desk, closer to a printed spec than to a product site, so density is calm and the reading column is narrow.

The world is recognisable with the words removed: a 2px ruled header strip carrying a document number (QT-<version> · alpha · <build date>), a left index rail, a 37rem text column, and numbered Notes in the right margin that come from markdown footnotes. Timing-diagram figures are drawn in inline SVG in the margin (Fig. 1 on the home page, Fig. 2 on the verdicts page) and are the one place the system moves.

Rejected on purpose: kicker lines above headings, coloured side-stripes, cards, decorative gradients, section numbers, and icon glyphs. Light only, by design: this is a printed-datasheet world read at a desk, and no dark scheme exists.
keyCharacteristics: White page, near-black ink, one blue (datasheet-blue), hairline rule borders, no radius anywhere.
State is carried by text, weight and rules, never by hue alone.
Three type voices: B612 for structure, Source Serif 4 for prose, Source Code Pro for code and values.
A fixed 37rem measure for prose; code blocks and tables use the full reading column.
A print stylesheet drops chrome and prints the column as a plain document.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue means "follow this", "you are here", or "this is a dimension". It is never used to signal status, and it is never the only carrier of meaning.

rules.name: The Text-Carries-State Rule
rules.body: Verdicts and states are written (PROVED, PROVED-UNDER, REFUTED, UNKNOWN) and set in weight or case. No red/green status colours exist in the system.

rules.name: The Fixed Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose width is 37rem, not ch, because ch widens on large headings and drifts the column. Code blocks and tables take the whole reading column.

rules.name: The Source Code Pro Rule
rules.body: Code is Source Code Pro, not B612 Mono. B612 Mono sets the period flush-left in a wide cell, so ff.default reads as "ff. default".

rules.name: The 12px Floor Rule
rules.body: No functional text is below 12px (0.75rem). Labels once at 10.56px were raised to this floor.

rules.name: The Rules-Not-Shadows Rule
rules.body: Separate with a 1px or 2px line, or the wash tone. A shadow is never the answer.

dos: Do use datasheet-blue only for links, the current location, dimensions and focus.
Do carry state in words, weight and rules so it survives greyscale and print.
Do keep prose at 37rem and give code and tables the full column.
Do keep every functional label at 12px or larger.
Do write code, flags and values in Source Code Pro and tables, labels and headings in B612.
Do gate any animation behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
donts: Don't add kicker or eyebrow lines above headings, section numbers, or icon glyphs.
Don't add coloured side-stripes, cards, decorative gradients, or drop shadows.
Don't introduce a second chromatic colour or red/green status colours.
Don't use B612 Mono for code, or set measure in ch.
Don't add a dark mode: the world is a printed datasheet read at a desk.
